headline.what_this_block_is: THE MEASURED PROFILE HAS BEEN RESET, AND THAT IS THE HONEST STATE. This block used to render an eleven-axis error attribution per analyst, computed on that analyst's own graded history. On 2026-07-31 all four analysts were re-architected onto DISJOINT feature slices and retrained; the history the old profile was computed from belongs to four different models. Serving it beside the new records would be describing one thing and measuring another. So the block reports the reset instead — and the previous reading was in any case a NULL: across 357 measured cells, nothing separated any analyst from its own baseline once the family was corrected for. The profile will be recomputed against the new analysts when their record is deep enough to attribute, which will take months, not days.

desk_calls.note: THE DESK'S CALLS, GRADED IN THEIR OWN LEDGER. This is NOT a betting record and must never be summed with one, shown beside one as a comparison, or described in units: a call has no price and no stake, so it has no ROI. It counts one row per game — the desk's view at the most informed wall it reached — and it exists to answer one question the product could not previously ask: when the desk says something, is it right? A CALL IS NOT A BET. This is the desk's directional view on the game — what it actually thinks — built from the four analysts' own reads, equal-weighted. It is NEVER staked, it NEVER enters games[].pick, it is never counted in the product record, and it cannot be sized. Whether we are betting this game is a separate question with a separate answer, at `we_are_betting` / `bet_action`, decided by the price gate alone and unchanged by anything here. The graded product remains games[].pick and only games[].pick; the desk's calls are graded in their own ledger, separately, from 2026-08-01.
desk_calls.honest_note: THE STANDING HYGIENE RULE APPLIES IN FULL. This ledger starts at 2026-08-01 and will take months to say anything. A hit rate here is not evidence of edge in either direction, and in particular a call that beats 50% is NOT an argument for loosening the price gate — the gate is what protects the product record and it does not move on this.
desk_calls.contract: THE DESK-CALL CONTRACT (2026-08-01). WHAT IT IS: a directional view on EVERY game — side, conviction, a probability and a one-line argument — built from the four analysts' own reads, equal-weighted (the measured house position: desk_fit's walk-forward refused a fitted combiner). SERVED AT games[].diamondedge.desk_call. WHAT IT IS NOT: A CALL IS NOT A BET. Whether we are betting a game is decided by the price gate alone and is served, unchanged, at games[].diamondedge.action (PLAY / LEAN / AVOID, where AVOID still means and only means that no bet was served) and at games[].pick. Every call row hard-stamps is_bet=False, staked=False, stake_units=None, playable=False, suggested_units=None, take=False, stars=None and pick_side=None, and those stamps are re-asserted on every write and every read; the module may write only its own three stores and refuses every served board and product ledger by name. THE VOCABULARY, and a reader can never mistake one axis for the other: `desk_call.call` is the CALL (STRONG/CLEAR/SLIGHT + OVER/UNDER), `desk_call.state` fuses both axes (CALL_AND_PLAY / CALL_AND_LEAN / CALL_NO_BET / CALL_NO_GAME / PENDING), `we_are_betting` is the bet in one boolean, and `why_no_bet` names the reason when it is false. GRADING: the graded product remains games[].pick and ONLY games[].pick. The desk's calls are graded in their own append-only ledger, one row per game at its most informed wall, from 2026-08-01, with no units and no ROI because a call has no price.
desk_calls.separated_from: record.overall / record.overall_playable, which are the graded product and are built from games[].pick alone

2026-08-08.rule_name: The Pitcher's Park, the Rested Arm and the Closer Up

voice.name: The Pitcher's Park, the Rested Arm and the Closer Up
paragraphs: This one lives on the ballpark, the starting pitching, and the bullpens. It is a 6-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds another of our models reading the over, a ballpark that has been taking runs away, and a visiting starter working on extra rest. Another of our models reading the over is the ordinary case for the over. The rest of it is not: A ballpark that has been taking runs away and a visiting starter working on extra rest are what you would normally write down the other way, and wanting both at once is the whole idea. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the conditions analyst is not strongly on the under, the visiting closer available for the ninth, and the ballpark is the biggest thing setting this game's run environment. Same shape, mirrored — the visiting closer available for the ninth is the obvious part and the conditions analyst is not strongly on the under is the part that cuts against it.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Jul 22 to Aug 7) it played 174 of the 221 games it saw, and it went 125-46-3. That is what it did on games already played — the same games that picked it out — and it is a count, not a rate to come.

voice.name: The Pitcher's Park, the Rested Arm and the Closer Up
paragraphs: This one lives on the ballpark, the starting pitching, and the bullpens. It is a 6-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds another of our models reading the over, a ballpark that has been taking runs away, and a visiting starter working on extra rest. Another of our models reading the over is the ordinary case for the over. The rest of it is not: A ballpark that has been taking runs away and a visiting starter working on extra rest are what you would normally write down the other way, and wanting both at once is the whole idea. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the conditions analyst is not strongly on the under, the visiting closer available for the ninth, and the ballpark is the biggest thing setting this game's run environment. Same shape, mirrored — the visiting closer available for the ninth is the obvious part and the conditions analyst is not strongly on the under is the part that cuts against it.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Jul 22 to Aug 7) it played 174 of the 221 games it saw, and it went 125-46-3. That is what it did on games already played — the same games that picked it out — and it is a count, not a rate to come.

supplemental_serve.what_this_is: OWNER-DIRECTED SUPPLEMENTAL PICKS. Leon adds these by hand from the expanded nightly engine (v2). They FILL games the desk did not pick and never override one. They are served pregame at a real price, graded under the same outcome-verification gate as every other pick, and counted in the record under source 'engine_v2_owner'.
supplemental_serve.admission_rules: A supplemental row is REFUSED, never silently dropped and never quietly applied. The two admission rules are re-checked on every payload build: the game must have no served pick already, and it must still be pregame with 30 minutes of margin. Once a row has been admitted it is served from the write-once as-served ledger and the gate is not re-run — a served pick never un-serves itself.

withdrawals.what_this_is: OWNER-DIRECTED WITHDRAWAL. Leon superseded a still-PREGAME served pick with a newer engine's verdict, so the board serves that game as a PASS. Nothing was edited or deleted: the original row is archived verbatim in state/superseded_picks_<date>.jsonl alongside the supersession, its reason, its authorisation and its timestamp. A withdrawal is refused outright once the game is inside the 30-minute pregame margin — after first pitch, choosing which open bet to keep is exactly what a public record may never do. Because the game was never decided, it leaves the day's denominator rather than entering it as a loss or a win.

board_coverage.multi_wall_note: SEATS FILL FROM THE MOST INFORMED WALL THAT HAS A READ. Until 2026-07-31 the four analysts priced a game ONLY where its T-3h frame existed, which left more than half of a live evening board with four empty seats for most of the day. They now price every wall from T-24h forward, each from a model fitted at that wall over the information that actually exists there, and a seat shows the best read available with the wall stamped on it. THIS IS NOT FORCED COVERAGE: no read is manufactured, the evidence floor refuses a read whose inputs are not populated, and a seat with nothing behind it stays empty and prints the reason.
board_coverage.note: Per-analyst read counts over the SERVED cards. The four reads come from analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date and nothing else, so `native` is every read and `coverage` is permanently 0 — FORCED COVERAGE IS RETIRED. It used to manufacture a fallback read for whichever of the four dismantled engines had frozen nothing on a game, which guaranteed a full board by construction. The v2 stream prices a game only where its T-3h feature frame exists, so a no-read is a real statement about the feed for that game and is counted here rather than filled in from a different model.

line_now_audit.note: line_now is the SAME full-game pregame totals market as the locked line, compared same-book or on the identical book-consensus-median basis, suppressed once the game starts, and refused when the implied move exceeds what a full-game total can do. Refusals appear here; they are never shipped as a move.

definition.max_score_why: the measure is strictly below 1 at any finite amount of evidence, so no pick is ever shown as 100
definition.formula: p = (for + 1) / (for + against + 2); confidence = min(99, round(100 * max(0, 2p - 1)))
definition.prior: uniform (Beta(1,1)) — the standard uninformative choice, pre-specified, not fitted to any board
definition.why_not: pick_strength divides by every seated strategy, abstentions included. On a 31-seat committee where the top pick draws about 4 seats that puts every pick under the 0.25 cut, so every pick reads 'lean' and the measure separates nothing. This measure divides by the seats that actually voted and uses the +1/+2 smoothing to keep a thin unanimous room below a deep one — which is the objection pick_strength raises against dividing by votes cast.

forge_strategy.plain_english_rule: Bet OVER when the park suppresses runs and the arms the away bullpen used yesterday is below 5 and both starters are known and the two starters' gap in days of rest (home minus away) is below 1. Otherwise bet UNDER when the conditions analyst's read was driven by the park and the desk's edge measured against how much the desk disagrees with itself is at least -1. Otherwise pass.
forge_strategy.search_scope: Every rule the search can write was applied, unchanged, to every game on every night of the window, and scored on one thing: how many more times it won than it lost. Nothing else was ranked on.
forge_strategy.summary_line: Today's board is one rule. It came out of last night's search with the best win-minus-loss record over the window, and it was frozen before the first game. Over the 17 nights it was chosen on (2026-07-22 to 2026-08-07), this rule went 129-50-3.
forge_strategy.selected_reason: Every rule the search can write was applied, unchanged, to every game on every night of the lookback window. The rule that finished with the best record of wins minus losses was frozen and applied to today's slate. The window ends before today, so no game on this board was part of choosing the rule.
forge_strategy.record_is_about_the_past_only: The record above is what this rule would have done on the games in its own lookback window — the same games that chose it. It is an in-sample count and a statement about the past. It is not a forecast, not an expected win rate, and not a claim about tonight's games.
forge_strategy.line_basis: The pick is served at the locked pregame line and its real price. A game with no line, or no price at that line, is not served at all.
forge_strategy.grading_policy: graded exactly like every other served pick, behind the outcome-verification gate; never re-graded, never restated
forge_strategy.tier_basis: One rule chose every pick on this board and it makes no distinction between them, so every forge pick carries the same display tier. There is no per-pick conviction to report.
forge_strategy.progressive_note: The rule is frozen before the day starts. Each game gets its call the moment its inputs land, against that same frozen rule — never a re-search, and never a different rule later in the day.

paragraphs: This one lives on the ballpark, the bullpens, and the shape of the matchup. It is a 5-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds a ballpark that has been taking runs away, nothing that amounts to a visiting bullpen emptied out yesterday, and nothing that amounts to the home starter working on more rest than his opposite number. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: this is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the ballpark is the biggest thing setting this game's run environment and the desk is not under the market by more than its own disagreement. Again the natural reading of those conditions is the over, and again it goes the other way.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Jul 22 to Aug 7) it played 182 of the 221 games it saw, and it went 129-50-3. That is what it did on games already played — the same games that picked it out — and it is a count, not a rate to come.

paragraphs: Right-hander Brady Singer takes the ball for the Reds at Nationals Park on Sunday, against the Nationals, with a sweep on the line for the hosts. Brad Lord gets the ball for the Nationals. Lord was untouchable in his last logged start: 2 1/3 shutout innings on 2 hits and 2 walks, with 1 strikeout in a 10-2 win at Boston on July 1. Singer (2-4 with a 4.43 ERA over his last 7 starts) gave up 3 runs on 5 hits over 6 innings last time out in a 5-4 win against the Athletics on Tuesday.
The lean here is the under. This number has sat on 9.5 since it opened. The ballpark here has been playing about 5% above league-average scoring over the last three years.

The rest of the card leans that way too: the Reds went to 2 relievers yesterday and Singer has walked 7% of the hitters he has faced across his last five starts. Their recent scoring has been running 0.8 runs a game short of tonight's total and the posted total is 0.6 runs higher than what this ballpark has typically supported.
The Nationals have scored 4.9 runs a game over their last fifteen, the Reds 3.9. The season series is 4-1 to the Nationals.

why: walk-forward, the fitted weights are not distinguishable from equal weighting (delta log-loss -0.00040, 95% CI [-0.00127, +0.00047] on 284 games over 22 days)
desk_fit.gate: adopt fitted weights only when the trailing window holds >= 300 graded games with >= 100 reads for every analyst AND the walk-forward log-loss improvement over equal weighting has a 95% day-clustered interval strictly better than zero

source.note: the v2 stream's own append-only GRADED LEDGER — the graded half of the write-once board that analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date() serves the desk chief, so the combiner and the chief describe the same desk. Read only; nothing here re-prices or re-grades. Pushes carry no outcome and are dropped, as are games whose analysts were priced at different lines and landed between them.
source.no_longer_read: v4/models/analyst_desk/history.parquet — the walk-forward reconstruction of the PREVIOUS four analysts (the price analyst the champion engine, the hitting analyst the v4 grid, the conditions analyst the simulator, the pitching analyst the simple-8 fundamentals). Those four were dismantled on 2026-07-31; a weight fitted on their behaviour is not a weight for the analysts it would be applied to. The file is left on disk untouched — nothing is deleted or restated — and is simply never opened by this module.
source.fence: no frame on or before 2026-06-30 — the four models were fitted through that date, so a frame at or before it would be a fit on training data

desk_fit.headline: Fitting the four analysts' disagreement-with-the-price over a rolling 30-day window does NOT beat weighting them equally: walk-forward over 284 games and 22 days the log-loss difference is -0.00040 (95% CI [-0.00127, +0.00047]). The desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS. Neither is the combined desk distinguishable from simply using the price.
desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.
caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

No analyst shows a positive edge on its own side and none is claimed (the four sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points). What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. Whether it carries edge is a question only the forward record answers.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A BET RULE. It re-fits every night over the trailing 30 days how each analyst's DISAGREEMENT WITH THE PRICE has related to results, scores that fit WALK-FORWARD (fit strictly on days before the day it is scored on, never on the days it is scored on), and compares it to two baselines: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are only ever ADOPTED when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting has an interval strictly better than zero AND the window carries enough reads to fit four weights. When it does not — which is the state today — the desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS and this block says so with the numbers, because presenting a fitted weight whose interval straddles the equal-weight baseline is presenting noise as insight. Nothing here gates, sizes or grades a bet: the +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet, and the combined probability is display only, graded nowhere.

coherence.note: THE BET IS `the_bet` and nothing else on this card is a bet. The desk's majority lean, the desk's weighted combination and the conditions analyst's predicted final score are three DISPLAY readings of the same game; each is reported here with whether it points the same way as the ticket. A voice pointing the other way is information, not a contradiction — none of them clears a price gate, and none of them is graded. The run line is a separate market and is never expected to agree with a total.

chief.rationale_line: We're on the under 9.5 at -110 (3★) on the price edge, with the desk split down the middle — two analysts each way. The split is context, not a veto.
chief.note: THE CHIEF (Leon, 2026-07-30; SEMANTICS REWRITTEN 2026-07-31): DiamondEdge's own PREGAME synthesis — the O/U call, the run-line call and the predicted final score, all against the LOCKED pregame line, with a rationale grounded in the MEASURED tables. THE COHERENCE RULE (the 2026-07-31 fix): when the engine SERVED A BET, the chief's O/U call IS that bet — same side, same number — and the action can never be AVOID. AVOID means, and only ever means, that no bet was served. The desk's disagreement with a served bet is real and is stated (desk_agreement + the rationale line), but it is stated as CONTEXT, never as 'we're passing' on a bet we are actually making. The chief remains PRESENTATION and ROUTING ONLY: the measured pattern table can change the language and move a displayed action DOWN one rung, never up, a PASS can never become a PLAY, and on a served bet the ladder bottoms out at LEAN. Betting stays with the +EV gate and the star system, exactly as before. predicted_score and desk_combined are display predictions, graded nowhere.

diamondedge.note: CONTINUITY: the underlying DiamondEdge pick machinery is UNCHANGED and its record continues unbroken — write-once walls, the +EV gate, stars, calibration and grading all run exactly as before, and `pick` is still the served object. The desk's ACTION is presentation logic layered on top. COHERENCE (2026-07-31 — the defect this replaced): the action used to be a four-way VOTE, so a card could serve a real staked bet and, in the same breath, tell the reader the desk was passing on it. It did exactly that on both served bets of 2026-07-31. AVOID now means, and only ever means, THAT NO BET WAS SERVED (pick.status != PICK); a served bet displays as PLAY or LEAN by its star tier, and the desk's disagreement — which is real and is worth reading — is carried in `desk_agreement` (ALIGNED|MIXED|AGAINST|PENDING) and said out loud in the rationale as CONTEXT, never as a veto. The rail is unchanged in the direction that matters: the synthesis can never manufacture a bet, a PASS can never become a PLAY, and no served pick was created, altered, re-graded or removed by any of this. synthesis_config_version stamps the measured config in force: v1 (2026-07-30, the competition workflow's verifier-upheld artifact, v4/models/analyst_desk/synthesis_config_v1.json) is explicitly PRESENTATION/ROUTING only — its own measurement found no consensus state distinguishable from a coin flip as a bet rule, so betting confidence remains solely the champion EV gate + star system. A stricter coupling (the synthesis actually gating which picks are served) would require a future config that measures and declares exactly that.

weather.as_of_basis: Every value is the T-3h forecast — retrieved before the wall the pick is made at, never an observation from during the game.

pick.star_tier: Rule pick — the day's rule called this side

confidence.what_it_is: One rule chose every pick on this board and makes no distinction between them, so there is no per-game vote to read. This is the rule's own win-loss record over its lookback window, on the same 0-100 scale — the same number for every pick on the board.
confidence.not_a_probability: A confidence of 90 does not mean a 90% chance of winning. This is a normalised measure of how strongly the evidence behind the pick leans one way, not a calibrated probability, an edge or a price. Nothing here claims a higher score wins more often; that is being tracked, not assumed.
confidence.counts_all_picks: Every pick counts in the record at every confidence score. This is a CUT of the served population, never a filter on it.

definition.max_score_why: the measure is strictly below 1 at any finite amount of evidence, so no pick is ever shown as 100
definition.formula: p = (for + 1) / (for + against + 2); confidence = min(99, round(100 * max(0, 2p - 1)))
definition.prior: uniform (Beta(1,1)) — the standard uninformative choice, pre-specified, not fitted to any board
definition.why_not: pick_strength divides by every seated strategy, abstentions included. On a 31-seat committee where the top pick draws about 4 seats that puts every pick under the 0.25 cut, so every pick reads 'lean' and the measure separates nothing. This measure divides by the seats that actually voted and uses the +1/+2 smoothing to keep a thin unanimous room below a deep one — which is the objection pick_strength raises against dividing by votes cast.
definition.note: A confidence of 90 does not mean a 90% chance of winning. This is a normalised measure of how strongly the evidence behind the pick leans one way, not a calibrated probability, an edge or a price. Nothing here claims a higher score wins more often; that is being tracked, not assumed.
definition.counts_all_picks: Every pick counts in the record at every confidence score. This is a CUT of the served population, never a filter on it.

confidence.rule: Bet OVER when the park suppresses runs and the arms the away bullpen used yesterday is below 5 and both starters are known and the two starters' gap in days of rest (home minus away) is below 1. paragraphs: This one lives on the ballpark, the bullpens, and the shape of the matchup. It is a 5-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds a ballpark that has been taking runs away, nothing that amounts to a visiting bullpen emptied out yesterday, and nothing that amounts to the home starter working on more rest than his opposite number. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: this is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the ballpark is the biggest thing setting this game's run environment and the desk is not under the market by more than its own disagreement. Again the natural reading of those conditions is the over, and again it goes the other way.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Jul 22 to Aug 7) it played 182 of the 221 games it saw, and it went 129-50-3. That is what it did on games already played — the same games that picked it out — and it is a count, not a rate to come.

desk_fit.headline: Fitting the four analysts' disagreement-with-the-price over a rolling 30-day window does NOT beat weighting them equally: walk-forward over 284 games and 22 days the log-loss difference is -0.00040 (95% CI [-0.00127, +0.00047]). The desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS. Neither is the combined desk distinguishable from simply using the price.
desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.
caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

No analyst shows a positive edge on its own side and none is claimed (the four sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points). What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. Whether it carries edge is a question only the forward record answers.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A BET RULE. It re-fits every night over the trailing 30 days how each analyst's DISAGREEMENT WITH THE PRICE has related to results, scores that fit WALK-FORWARD (fit strictly on days before the day it is scored on, never on the days it is scored on), and compares it to two baselines: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are only ever ADOPTED when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting has an interval strictly better than zero AND the window carries enough reads to fit four weights. When it does not — which is the state today — the desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS and this block says so with the numbers, because presenting a fitted weight whose interval straddles the equal-weight baseline is presenting noise as insight. Nothing here gates, sizes or grades a bet: the +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet, and the combined probability is display only, graded nowhere.

chief.note: THE CHIEF (Leon, 2026-07-30; SEMANTICS REWRITTEN 2026-07-31): DiamondEdge's own PREGAME synthesis — the O/U call, the run-line call and the predicted final score, all against the LOCKED pregame line, with a rationale grounded in the MEASURED tables. THE COHERENCE RULE (the 2026-07-31 fix): when the engine SERVED A BET, the chief's O/U call IS that bet — same side, same number — and the action can never be AVOID. AVOID means, and only ever means, that no bet was served. The desk's disagreement with a served bet is real and is stated (desk_agreement + the rationale line), but it is stated as CONTEXT, never as 'we're passing' on a bet we are actually making. The chief remains PRESENTATION and ROUTING ONLY: the measured pattern table can change the language and move a displayed action DOWN one rung, never up, a PASS can never become a PLAY, and on a served bet the ladder bottoms out at LEAN. Betting stays with the +EV gate and the star system, exactly as before. predicted_score and desk_combined are display predictions, graded nowhere.

diamondedge.note: CONTINUITY: the underlying DiamondEdge pick machinery is UNCHANGED and its record continues unbroken — write-once walls, the +EV gate, stars, calibration and grading all run exactly as before, and `pick` is still the served object. The desk's ACTION is presentation logic layered on top. COHERENCE (2026-07-31 — the defect this replaced): the action used to be a four-way VOTE, so a card could serve a real staked bet and, in the same breath, tell the reader the desk was passing on it. It did exactly that on both served bets of 2026-07-31. AVOID now means, and only ever means, THAT NO BET WAS SERVED (pick.status != PICK); a served bet displays as PLAY or LEAN by its star tier, and the desk's disagreement — which is real and is worth reading — is carried in `desk_agreement` (ALIGNED|MIXED|AGAINST|PENDING) and said out loud in the rationale as CONTEXT, never as a veto. paragraphs: This one lives on the ballpark, the bullpens, and the shape of the matchup. It is a 5-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds a ballpark that has been taking runs away, nothing that amounts to a visiting bullpen emptied out yesterday, and nothing that amounts to the home starter working on more rest than his opposite number. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: this is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the ballpark is the biggest thing setting this game's run environment and the desk is not under the market by more than its own disagreement. Again the natural reading of those conditions is the over, and again it goes the other way.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Jul 22 to Aug 7) it played 182 of the 221 games it saw, and it went 129-50-3. That is what it did on games already played — the same games that picked it out — and it is a count, not a rate to come.

source.no_longer_read: v4/models/analyst_desk/history.parquet — the walk-forward reconstruction of the PREVIOUS four analysts (the price analyst the champion engine, the hitting analyst the v4 grid, the conditions analyst the simulator, the pitching analyst the simple-8 fundamentals). Those four were dismantled on 2026-07-31; a weight fitted on their behaviour is not a weight for the analysts it would be applied to. The file is left on disk untouched — nothing is deleted or restated — and is simply never opened by this module.

desk_fit.headline: Fitting the four analysts' disagreement-with-the-price over a rolling 30-day window does NOT beat weighting them equally: walk-forward over 284 games and 22 days the log-loss difference is -0.00040 (95% CI [-0.00127, +0.00047]). The desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS. Neither is the combined desk distinguishable from simply using the price.
desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.
caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

No analyst shows a positive edge on its own side and none is claimed (the four sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points). What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. Whether it carries edge is a question only the forward record answers.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A BET RULE. It re-fits every night over the trailing 30 days how each analyst's DISAGREEMENT WITH THE PRICE has related to results, scores that fit WALK-FORWARD (fit strictly on days before the day it is scored on, never on the days it is scored on), and compares it to two baselines: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are only ever ADOPTED when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting has an interval strictly better than zero AND the window carries enough reads to fit four weights. When it does not — which is the state today — the desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS and this block says so with the numbers, because presenting a fitted weight whose interval straddles the equal-weight baseline is presenting noise as insight. Nothing here gates, sizes or grades a bet: the +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet, and the combined probability is display only, graded nowhere.

The run line is a separate market and is never expected to agree with a total.

paragraphs: This one lives on the ballpark, the bullpens, and the shape of the matchup. It is a 5-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds a ballpark that has been taking runs away, nothing that amounts to a visiting bullpen emptied out yesterday, and nothing that amounts to the home starter working on more rest than his opposite number. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: this is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the ballpark is the biggest thing setting this game's run environment and the desk is not under the market by more than its own disagreement. Again the natural reading of those conditions is the over, and again it goes the other way.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Jul 22 to Aug 7) it played 182 of the 221 games it saw, and it went 129-50-3. That is what it did on games already played — the same games that picked it out — and it is a count, not a rate to come.

The Yankees have scored 3.0 runs a game over their last fifteen, the Braves 4.1. The Yankees have won both meetings between them this season.

desk_fit.headline: Fitting the four analysts' disagreement-with-the-price over a rolling 30-day window does NOT beat weighting them equally: walk-forward over 284 games and 22 days the log-loss difference is -0.00040 (95% CI [-0.00127, +0.00047]). The desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS. Neither is the combined desk distinguishable from simply using the price.
desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.
caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

No analyst shows a positive edge on its own side and none is claimed (the four sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points). What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. Whether it carries edge is a question only the forward record answers.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A BET RULE. It re-fits every night over the trailing 30 days how each analyst's DISAGREEMENT WITH THE PRICE has related to results, scores that fit WALK-FORWARD (fit strictly on days before the day it is scored on, never on the days it is scored on), and compares it to two baselines: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are only ever ADOPTED when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting has an interval strictly better than zero AND the window carries enough reads to fit four weights. When it does not — which is the state today — the desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS and this block says so with the numbers, because presenting a fitted weight whose interval straddles the equal-weight baseline is presenting noise as insight. Nothing here gates, sizes or grades a bet: the +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet, and the combined probability is display only, graded nowhere.

desk_combined.note: the desk's weighted combination of the four analysts' disagreement with the price. DISPLAY ONLY — it is graded nowhere, it never changes the action, and it is not an edge: walk-forward it does not beat the price. Read it as 'where the desk collectively sits versus the number'.

coherence.note: THE BET IS `the_bet` and nothing else on this card is a bet. The desk's majority lean, the desk's weighted combination and the conditions analyst's predicted final score are three DISPLAY readings of the same game; each is reported here with whether it points the same way as the ticket. A voice pointing the other way is information, not a contradiction — none of them clears a price gate, and none of them is graded. The run line is a separate market and is never expected to agree with a total.

chief.rationale_line: We're on the under 8.5 at -105 (3★) on the price edge, with the desk split down the middle — two analysts each way. The split is context, not a veto.
chief.note: THE CHIEF (Leon, 2026-07-30; SEMANTICS REWRITTEN 2026-07-31): DiamondEdge's own PREGAME synthesis — the O/U call, the run-line call and the predicted final score, all against the LOCKED pregame line, with a rationale grounded in the MEASURED tables. THE COHERENCE RULE (the 2026-07-31 fix): when the engine SERVED A BET, the chief's O/U call IS that bet — same side, same number — and the action can never be AVOID. AVOID means, and only ever means, that no bet was served. The desk's disagreement with a served bet is real and is stated (desk_agreement + the rationale line), but it is stated as CONTEXT, never as 'we're passing' on a bet we are actually making. The chief remains PRESENTATION and ROUTING ONLY: the measured pattern table can change the language and move a displayed action DOWN one rung, never up, a PASS can never become a PLAY, and on a served bet the ladder bottoms out at LEAN. diamondedge.note: CONTINUITY: the underlying DiamondEdge pick machinery is UNCHANGED and its record continues unbroken — write-once walls, the +EV gate, stars, calibration and grading all run exactly as before, and `pick` is still the served object. The desk's ACTION is presentation logic layered on top. COHERENCE (2026-07-31 — the defect this replaced): the action used to be a four-way VOTE, so a card could serve a real staked bet and, in the same breath, tell the reader the desk was passing on it. It did exactly that on both served bets of 2026-07-31. AVOID now means, and only ever means, THAT NO BET WAS SERVED (pick.status != PICK); a served bet displays as PLAY or LEAN by its star tier, and the desk's disagreement — which is real and is worth reading — is carried in `desk_agreement` (ALIGNED|MIXED|AGAINST|PENDING) and said out loud in the rationale as CONTEXT, never as a veto. The rail is unchanged in the direction that matters: the synthesis can never manufacture a bet, a PASS can never become a PLAY, and no served pick was created, altered, re-graded or removed by any of this. synthesis_config_version stamps the measured config in force: v1 (2026-07-30, the competition workflow's verifier-upheld artifact, v4/models/analyst_desk/synthesis_config_v1.json) is explicitly PRESENTATION/ROUTING only — its own measurement found no consensus state distinguishable from a coin flip as a bet rule, so betting confidence remains solely the champion EV gate + star system. paragraphs: This one lives on the ballpark, the bullpens, and the shape of the matchup. It is a 5-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds a ballpark that has been taking runs away, nothing that amounts to a visiting bullpen emptied out yesterday, and nothing that amounts to the home starter working on more rest than his opposite number. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: this is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the ballpark is the biggest thing setting this game's run environment and the desk is not under the market by more than its own disagreement. Again the natural reading of those conditions is the over, and again it goes the other way.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Jul 22 to Aug 7) it played 182 of the 221 games it saw, and it went 129-50-3. That is what it did on games already played — the same games that picked it out — and it is a count, not a rate to come.

source.no_longer_read: v4/models/analyst_desk/history.parquet — the walk-forward reconstruction of the PREVIOUS four analysts (the price analyst the champion engine, the hitting analyst the v4 grid, the conditions analyst the simulator, the pitching analyst the simple-8 fundamentals). Those four were dismantled on 2026-07-31; a weight fitted on their behaviour is not a weight for the analysts it would be applied to. source.fence: no frame on or before 2026-06-30 — the four models were fitted through that date, so a frame at or before it would be a fit on training data

desk_fit.headline: Fitting the four analysts' disagreement-with-the-price over a rolling 30-day window does NOT beat weighting them equally: walk-forward over 284 games and 22 days the log-loss difference is -0.00040 (95% CI [-0.00127, +0.00047]). The desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS. Neither is the combined desk distinguishable from simply using the price.
desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.
caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

No analyst shows a positive edge on its own side and none is claimed (the four sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points). What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. Whether it carries edge is a question only the forward record answers.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A BET RULE. It re-fits every night over the trailing 30 days how each analyst's DISAGREEMENT WITH THE PRICE has related to results, scores that fit WALK-FORWARD (fit strictly on days before the day it is scored on, never on the days it is scored on), and compares it to two baselines: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are only ever ADOPTED when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting has an interval strictly better than zero AND the window carries enough reads to fit four weights. When it does not — which is the state today — the desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS and this block says so with the numbers, because presenting a fitted weight whose interval straddles the equal-weight baseline is presenting noise as insight. Nothing here gates, sizes or grades a bet: the +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet, and the combined probability is display only, graded nowhere.

desk_combined.note: the desk's weighted combination of the four analysts' disagreement with the price. DISPLAY ONLY — it is graded nowhere, it never changes the action, and it is not an edge: walk-forward it does not beat the price. Read it as 'where the desk collectively sits versus the number'.

coherence.note: THE BET IS `the_bet` and nothing else on this card is a bet. The desk's majority lean, the desk's weighted combination and the conditions analyst's predicted final score are three DISPLAY readings of the same game; each is reported here with whether it points the same way as the ticket. A voice pointing the other way is information, not a contradiction — none of them clears a price gate, and none of them is graded. The run line is a separate market and is never expected to agree with a total.

chief.note: THE CHIEF (Leon, 2026-07-30; SEMANTICS REWRITTEN 2026-07-31): DiamondEdge's own PREGAME synthesis — the O/U call, the run-line call and the predicted final score, all against the LOCKED pregame line, with a rationale grounded in the MEASURED tables. THE COHERENCE RULE (the 2026-07-31 fix): when the engine SERVED A BET, the chief's O/U call IS that bet — same side, same number — and the action can never be AVOID. AVOID means, and only ever means, that no bet was served. The desk's disagreement with a served bet is real and is stated (desk_agreement + the rationale line), but it is stated as CONTEXT, never as 'we're passing' on a bet we are actually making. The chief remains PRESENTATION and ROUTING ONLY: the measured pattern table can change the language and move a displayed action DOWN one rung, never up, a PASS can never become a PLAY, and on a served bet the ladder bottoms out at LEAN. Betting stays with the +EV gate and the star system, exactly as before. predicted_score and desk_combined are display predictions, graded nowhere.

diamondedge.note: CONTINUITY: the underlying DiamondEdge pick machinery is UNCHANGED and its record continues unbroken — write-once walls, the +EV gate, stars, calibration and grading all run exactly as before, and `pick` is still the served object. The desk's ACTION is presentation logic layered on top. COHERENCE (2026-07-31 — the defect this replaced): the action used to be a four-way VOTE, so a card could serve a real staked bet and, in the same breath, tell the reader the desk was passing on it. It did exactly that on both served bets of 2026-07-31. AVOID now means, and only ever means, THAT NO BET WAS SERVED (pick.status != PICK); a served bet displays as PLAY or LEAN by its star tier, and the desk's disagreement — which is real and is worth reading — is carried in `desk_agreement` (ALIGNED|MIXED|AGAINST|PENDING) and said out loud in the rationale as CONTEXT, never as a veto. The rail is unchanged in the direction that matters: the synthesis can never manufacture a bet, a PASS can never become a PLAY, and no served pick was created, altered, re-graded or removed by any of this. synthesis_config_version stamps the measured config in force: v1 (2026-07-30, the competition workflow's verifier-upheld artifact, v4/models/analyst_desk/synthesis_config_v1.json) is explicitly PRESENTATION/ROUTING only — its own measurement found no consensus state distinguishable from a coin flip as a bet rule, so betting confidence remains solely the champion EV gate + star system. A stricter coupling (the synthesis actually gating which picks are served) would require a future config that measures and declares exactly that.

paragraphs: This one lives on the ballpark, the bullpens, and the shape of the matchup. It is a 5-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds a ballpark that has been taking runs away, nothing that amounts to a visiting bullpen emptied out yesterday, and nothing that amounts to the home starter working on more rest than his opposite number. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: this is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the ballpark is the biggest thing setting this game's run environment and the desk is not under the market by more than its own disagreement. Again the natural reading of those conditions is the over, and again it goes the other way.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Jul 22 to Aug 7) it played 182 of the 221 games it saw, and it went 129-50-3. That is what it did on games already played — the same games that picked it out — and it is a count, not a rate to come.

paragraphs: The Angels and the Marlins have split the first 2 games of this series at loanDepot park on Sunday, and this one settles it. Grayson Rodriguez (1-2 with a 6.00 ERA over his last 7 starts) starts for the Angels. Rodriguez went 7 innings last time out, giving up 2 runs on 3 hits with 1 walk and 6 strikeouts in a 3-1 loss at Baltimore on Tuesday. Ryan Gusto (0-2 with a 5.16 ERA over his last 7 starts) opposes him for the Marlins, and he gave up 1 run on 5 hits over 6 innings last time out in a 4-2 loss at Atlanta on Tuesday.
DiamondEdge sides with the under on this one. This number has sat on 8.5 since it opened. The ballpark here has been playing about 3% above league-average scoring over the last three years.

The supporting numbers point the same way: the Angels went to 1 reliever yesterday and Gusto has walked 4% of the hitters he has faced across his last five starts. The Angels have been reaching base at a .291 clip.
The Marlins have scored 5.7 runs a game over their last fifteen, the Angels 4.0. Each of them has taken 1 of the 2 they have played this season.

why: walk-forward, the fitted weights are not distinguishable from equal weighting (delta log-loss -0.00040, 95% CI [-0.00127, +0.00047] on 284 games over 22 days)
desk_fit.gate: adopt fitted weights only when the trailing window holds >= 300 graded games with >= 100 reads for every analyst AND the walk-forward log-loss improvement over equal weighting has a 95% day-clustered interval strictly better than zero

source.note: the v2 stream's own append-only GRADED LEDGER — the graded half of the write-once board that analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date() serves the desk chief, so the combiner and the chief describe the same desk. Read only; nothing here re-prices or re-grades. Pushes carry no outcome and are dropped, as are games whose analysts were priced at different lines and landed between them.
source.no_longer_read: v4/models/analyst_desk/history.parquet — the walk-forward reconstruction of the PREVIOUS four analysts (the price analyst the champion engine, the hitting analyst the v4 grid, the conditions analyst the simulator, the pitching analyst the simple-8 fundamentals). Those four were dismantled on 2026-07-31; a weight fitted on their behaviour is not a weight for the analysts it would be applied to. The file is left on disk untouched — nothing is deleted or restated — and is simply never opened by this module.
source.fence: no frame on or before 2026-06-30 — the four models were fitted through that date, so a frame at or before it would be a fit on training data

desk_fit.headline: Fitting the four analysts' disagreement-with-the-price over a rolling 30-day window does NOT beat weighting them equally: walk-forward over 284 games and 22 days the log-loss difference is -0.00040 (95% CI [-0.00127, +0.00047]). The desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS. Neither is the combined desk distinguishable from simply using the price.
desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.
caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

No analyst shows a positive edge on its own side and none is claimed (the four sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points). What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. Whether it carries edge is a question only the forward record answers.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A BET RULE. It re-fits every night over the trailing 30 days how each analyst's DISAGREEMENT WITH THE PRICE has related to results, scores that fit WALK-FORWARD (fit strictly on days before the day it is scored on, never on the days it is scored on), and compares it to two baselines: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are only ever ADOPTED when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting has an interval strictly better than zero AND the window carries enough reads to fit four weights. When it does not — which is the state today — the desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS and this block says so with the numbers, because presenting a fitted weight whose interval straddles the equal-weight baseline is presenting noise as insight. Nothing here gates, sizes or grades a bet: the +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet, and the combined probability is display only, graded nowhere.

desk_combined.note: the desk's weighted combination of the four analysts' disagreement with the price. DISPLAY ONLY — it is graded nowhere, it never changes the action, and it is not an edge: walk-forward it does not beat the price. Read it as 'where the desk collectively sits versus the number'.

coherence.note: THE BET IS `the_bet` and nothing else on this card is a bet. The desk's majority lean, the desk's weighted combination and the conditions analyst's predicted final score are three DISPLAY readings of the same game; each is reported here with whether it points the same way as the ticket. A voice pointing the other way is information, not a contradiction — none of them clears a price gate, and none of them is graded. The run line is a separate market and is never expected to agree with a total.

chief.note: THE CHIEF (Leon, 2026-07-30; SEMANTICS REWRITTEN 2026-07-31): DiamondEdge's own PREGAME synthesis — the O/U call, the run-line call and the predicted final score, all against the LOCKED pregame line, with a rationale grounded in the MEASURED tables. THE COHERENCE RULE (the 2026-07-31 fix): when the engine SERVED A BET, the chief's O/U call IS that bet — same side, same number — and the action can never be AVOID. AVOID means, and only ever means, that no bet was served. The desk's disagreement with a served bet is real and is stated (desk_agreement + the rationale line), but it is stated as CONTEXT, never as 'we're passing' on a bet we are actually making. The chief remains PRESENTATION and ROUTING ONLY: the measured pattern table can change the language and move a displayed action DOWN one rung, never up, a PASS can never become a PLAY, and on a served bet the ladder bottoms out at LEAN. Betting stays with the +EV gate and the star system, exactly as before. predicted_score and desk_combined are display predictions, graded nowhere.

diamondedge.note: CONTINUITY: the underlying DiamondEdge pick machinery is UNCHANGED and its record continues unbroken — write-once walls, the +EV gate, stars, calibration and grading all run exactly as before, and `pick` is still the served object. The desk's ACTION is presentation logic layered on top. COHERENCE (2026-07-31 — the defect this replaced): the action used to be a four-way VOTE, so a card could serve a real staked bet and, in the same breath, tell the reader the desk was passing on it. It did exactly that on both served bets of 2026-07-31. AVOID now means, and only ever means, THAT NO BET WAS SERVED (pick.status != PICK); a served bet displays as PLAY or LEAN by its star tier, and the desk's disagreement — which is real and is worth reading — is carried in `desk_agreement` (ALIGNED|MIXED|AGAINST|PENDING) and said out loud in the rationale as CONTEXT, never as a veto. The rail is unchanged in the direction that matters: the synthesis can never manufacture a bet, a PASS can never become a PLAY, and no served pick was created, altered, re-graded or removed by any of this. synthesis_config_version stamps the measured config in force: v1 (2026-07-30, the competition workflow's verifier-upheld artifact, v4/models/analyst_desk/synthesis_config_v1.json) is explicitly PRESENTATION/ROUTING only — its own measurement found no consensus state distinguishable from a coin flip as a bet rule, so betting confidence remains solely the champion EV gate + star system. A stricter coupling (the synthesis actually gating which picks are served) would require a future config that measures and declares exactly that.

pick.star_tier: Rule pick — the day's rule called this side

confidence.what_it_is: One rule chose every pick on this board and makes no distinction between them, so there is no per-game vote to read. This is the rule's own win-loss record over its lookback window, on the same 0-100 scale — the same number for every pick on the board.
confidence.not_a_probability: A confidence of 90 does not mean a 90% chance of winning. This is a normalised measure of how strongly the evidence behind the pick leans one way, not a calibrated probability, an edge or a price. Nothing here claims a higher score wins more often; that is being tracked, not assumed.
confidence.counts_all_picks: Every pick counts in the record at every confidence score. This is a CUT of the served population, never a filter on it.

definition.max_score_why: the measure is strictly below 1 at any finite amount of evidence, so no pick is ever shown as 100
definition.formula: p = (for + 1) / (for + against + 2); confidence = min(99, round(100 * max(0, 2p - 1)))
definition.prior: uniform (Beta(1,1)) — the standard uninformative choice, pre-specified, not fitted to any board
definition.why_not: pick_strength divides by every seated strategy, abstentions included. On a 31-seat committee where the top pick draws about 4 seats that puts every pick under the 0.25 cut, so every pick reads 'lean' and the measure separates nothing. This measure divides by the seats that actually voted and uses the +1/+2 smoothing to keep a thin unanimous room below a deep one — which is the objection pick_strength raises against dividing by votes cast.

confidence.rule: Bet OVER when the park suppresses runs and the arms the away bullpen used yesterday is below 5 and both starters are known and the two starters' gap in days of rest (home minus away) is below 1. Otherwise bet UNDER when the conditions analyst's read was driven by the park and the desk's edge measured against how much the desk disagrees with itself is at least -1. Otherwise pass.
confidence.pushes_excluded: a push decided nothing, so it is not counted for or against; it is reported here so the record still adds up
confidence.evidence_is_in_sample: This is what the rule would have done on the games in its own lookback window — the same games that chose it. It is an in-sample count and a statement about the past. It is not a forecast and not a claim about tonight's games.
confidence.no_per_game_conviction: One rule chose every pick on this board and makes no distinction between them, so this number is the same for all of them. It does not say this particular game is a better bet than the one beside it.

pick_rating.basis_label: How squarely this game fits tonight's rule
pick_rating.cuts_basis: the tertiles of the reference the score is a percentile of — three bands that the reference population fills evenly by construction
pick_rating.what_it_is: How squarely this game sits inside the rule that picked it: the margin by which it clears the tightest of that clause's own thresholds, placed against the games the same clause fired on over the window that chose the rule. A higher number is a deeper instance of tonight's rule — not a better price and not a likelier win.
pick_rating.summary: How deep inside tonight's rule this game sits, against the games the same rule fired on. Not a price and not a likelier win.
pick_rating.caveat: This is a description of the game against the rule, not a forecast. Nothing here has been checked against outcomes, and no claim is made that a deeper instance of a rule wins more often.
pick_rating.not_a_forecast: The stars rate the pick against the thing that chose it. They are not a probability, not an edge, and not a claim about how often a three-star pick wins.

detail.what_it_is: How squarely this game sits inside the rule that picked it: the margin by which it clears the tightest of that clause's own thresholds, placed against the games the same clause fired on over the window that chose the rule. A higher number is a deeper instance of tonight's rule — not a better price and not a likelier win.
detail.summary: How deep inside tonight's rule this game sits, against the games the same rule fired on. Not a price and not a likelier win.
detail.clearance_units: robust spreads of each feature over the rule's own window (iqr_then_mad)
detail.reference: the games this same clause selected inside the rule's own lookback window
detail.reference_is_within_clause_why: a clause with three numeric conditions produces a smaller minimum than a clause with one, by construction — so a game is placed against the games its OWN clause fired on, not against the whole board's
detail.not_a_forecast: This is a description of the game against the rule, not a forecast. Nothing here has been checked against outcomes, and no claim is made that a deeper instance of a rule wins more often.
detail.reference_is_in_sample: The games this is measured against are the games in the rule's own lookback window — the same games that chose the rule. The comparison is in-sample and is a statement about the past.
detail.not_the_confidence: This is not the pick confidence and does not replace it. The confidence on a forge pick is the rule's own win-loss record over its window, which is the same number for every pick on the board; this one differs from game to game. They are different measures with different names, and neither is on the other's scale.

forge_strategy.search_scope: Every rule the search can write was applied, unchanged, to every game on every night of the window, and scored on one thing: how many more times it won than it lost. Nothing else was ranked on.
forge_strategy.summary_line: Today's board is one rule. It came out of last night's search with the best win-minus-loss record over the window, and it was frozen before the first game. Over the 17 nights it was chosen on (2026-07-22 to 2026-08-07), this rule went 129-50-3.
forge_strategy.selected_reason: Every rule the search can write was applied, unchanged, to every game on every night of the lookback window. The rule that finished with the best record of wins minus losses was frozen and applied to today's slate. The window ends before today, so no game on this board was part of choosing the rule.
forge_strategy.record_is_about_the_past_only: The record above is what this rule would have done on the games in its own lookback window — the same games that chose it. It is an in-sample count and a statement about the past. It is not a forecast, not an expected win rate, and not a claim about tonight's games.
forge_strategy.line_basis: The pick is served at the locked pregame line and its real price. A game with no line, or no price at that line, is not served at all.
forge_strategy.grading_policy: graded exactly like every other served pick, behind the outcome-verification gate; never re-graded, never restated
forge_strategy.tier_basis: One rule chose every pick on this board and it makes no distinction between them, so every forge pick carries the same display tier. There is no per-pick conviction to report.
forge_strategy.progressive_note: The rule is frozen before the day starts. Each game gets its call the moment its inputs land, against that same frozen rule — never a re-search, and never a different rule later in the day.

voice.name: The Pitcher's Park
voice.name_basis: generated from the rule's own conditions — a different rule wins the search every night, so the name is derived, never written by hand
paragraphs: This one lives on the ballpark, the bullpens, and the shape of the matchup. It is a 5-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds a ballpark that has been taking runs away, nothing that amounts to a visiting bullpen emptied out yesterday, and nothing that amounts to the home starter working on more rest than his opposite number. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: this is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the ballpark is the biggest thing setting this game's run environment and the desk is not under the market by more than its own disagreement. Again the natural reading of those conditions is the over, and again it goes the other way.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Jul 22 to Aug 7) it played 182 of the 221 games it saw, and it went 129-50-3. That is what it did on games already played — the same games that picked it out — and it is a count, not a rate to come.

paragraphs: The Twins and the Brewers close out their series at American Family Field on Sunday. Connor Prielipp (1-2 with a 4.23 ERA over his last 7 starts) goes for the Twins. Prielipp went 5 1/3 innings last time out, giving up 3 runs on 4 hits with 4 walks and 5 strikeouts in a 4-3 loss at Seattle on Aug. 1. Jacob Misiorowski (3-3 with a 2.25 ERA over his last 7 starts) answers for the Brewers, and he gave up 2 runs on 2 hits over 7 innings last time out in a 3-0 loss at Los Angeles on Sunday.
Our call on this game is the over. The total sits at 7 now, down from the 7.5 it opened at. The ballpark here has been playing about 5% below league-average scoring over the last three years.

The same conclusion turns up elsewhere: the two bullpens have thrown 21.3 innings between them over three days and Prielipp has walked 8% of the hitters he has faced across his last five starts. Their recent scoring has been running 3.1 runs a game clear of tonight's total and the posted total is 1.1 runs lower than what this ballpark has typically supported.
The Brewers have scored 4.2 runs a game over their last fifteen, the Twins 5.9. The Brewers have won 3 of the 5 meetings between them this season.
